YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO “ATTN: CITY COUNCIL,” ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE, CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY WATCH THE MEETING LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV.
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. IT WOULD BE APPRECIATED IF COMMUNICATIONS OF PUBLIC COMMENTS RELATED TO ITEMS ON THE AGENDA, OR ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA, ARE PROVIDED PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE MEETING. IF THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE, EVERY EFFORT WILL BE MADE TO ATTEMPT TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING. TOWARDS THIS END, THE MAYOR WILL ENDEAVOR TO TAKE A BRIEF PAUSE BEFORE ACTION IS TAKEN ON ANY AGENDA ITEM TO ALLOW THE CITY CLERK TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS, AND SHARE ANY E-COMMENTS RECEIVED DURING THE MEETING.

LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  May 26, 2020
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:55 p.m. on May 26,
2020, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine,
California; Mayor Shea presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox*
  Councilmember:  Farrah N. Khan
  Councilmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor:  Mike Carroll*
  Mayor:  Christina Shea

  * via teleconference

Prior to the Pledge of Allegiance, Mayor Shea announced that the meeting was broadcast
live on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and
livestreamed online at cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and
prevent the spread of COVID-19, the e-comment feature had been extended for all agenda
items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments through the
public comment portion of each item and would be included as part of the official record.
She also assured the community that the City of Irvine was adhering to the Governor’s
Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout City Hall by sanitizing surfaces and
equipment, as well as wearing face masks.
 City Council Minutes  May 26, 2020

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Shea led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Graham McGuinness from Woodbridge Community Church in Irvine provided the
  invocation.

  1.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITION

  1.1  Commend Tanaka Farms for Outstanding Community Service

  Mayor Shea presented, a commendation to Tanaka Farms for contributing
  to local farmers and donating thousands of pounds of fresh produce to
  South County Outreach and Irvine’s Families Forward. Councilmember
  Fox also provided a brief history on Tanaka Farms and expressed her
  appreciation for its outstanding community service.

  CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Khan made the following announcements:

  •  On Memorial Day, M.T.O. Shahmaghsoudi School of Islamic Sufism Center in Irvine
  honored veterans by preparing and delivering 600 grocery bags with food items and
  care packages to the V.A. Center.

  •  The Smiles Project in Irvine, which has been making cards for seniors, health care
  workers, and teachers, will now be collecting feminine hygiene products for women
  in need on Friday, June 5 from 3 to 4 p.m. at Heritage and University Park Libraries.
  Naturalena Brands, a local business in Irvine that manufactures feminine hygiene
  products, will also be joining the effort. Monetary donations can be made to the
  Smiles Project through its Facebook or Instagram pages.

  •  The Orange County Mosquito and Vector Control District (District) in which
  Councilmember Khan serves as the City’s liaison, recently held its first virtual meeting
  to discuss services offered by the District.

  Councilmember Kuo expressed his appreciation to Mayor Shea for representing the City of
  Irvine by attending the Orange County Board of Supervisors’ meeting earlier in the day; and
  also expressed his appreciation to Senior Public Safety Assistant Christine Tully, City
  Manager Russo, Public Safety staff, members of the Irvine Community Emergency

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  May 26, 2020

  Response Team, and others, who helped assemble and distribute hand sanitizer to over
  500 families.

  Vice Mayor Carroll announced that Mr. and Mrs. Wing Chow had graciously donated $200
  to the City of Irvine’s General Fund to offset the projected $22 million deficit due to the
  COVID-19 pandemic, and expressed his appreciation for their thoughtfulness and
  generosity.

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

  •  Noted her attendance at the Orange County Board of Supervisors meeting to
  advocate for funding for small businesses in Irvine, requesting that the County
  provide $75 million in CARES Act funding to support a Business Recovery Grant
  program as proposed by Supervisors Donald P. Wagner and Michelle Steel. The
  proposal would have provided direct funding to all Orange County cities to quickly
  provide much needed funds to small businesses; however, the Board decided to vote
  in a different direction and created a program to be administered by a third party.
  Supervisor Wagner stated that he would split funding in the Third District based on
  population for small businesses. Additional information will be provided later in the
  week by Supervisor Wagner.

  •  Irvine’s parks have been ranked the best in California and seventh best in the country
  by the Trust for Public Land. The Trust for Public Land’s “ParkScore Index” is the
  most comprehensive evaluation of park access and quality in the 100 largest cities in
  America. This year marks the fifth consecutive year that Irvine’s park system has
  ranked among the top ten. Irvine earned perfect scores in park spending per resident
  and basketball hoops per 10,000 residents, with high marks also earned in
  community centers and playgrounds. The ParkScore Index noted that 82% of Irvine
  parks are within a ten-minute walk of each residence, well above the national median
  of 72%. To find a complete list of City parks, visit cityofirvine.org/parks.

  •  The community is invited to participate in an “Irvine Neighbors Helping Irvine
  Neighbors” drive-through food collection event benefitting Families Forward on
  Saturday, June 6 from 9 a.m. to noon at the Orange County Great Park, Lot 2. Since
  social distancing measures went into effect in March, Families Forward has served
  more than 20,000 individuals with its Drive-Thru Food Assistance Program, which
  would not be possible without support from the community. For information and a list
  of items that are most in need, visit families-forward.org.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  May 26, 2020

  2.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  City Clerk Perry noted that Item 2.2 included proclamations that were very important
  to members of the community, and unfortunately, due to the pandemic, the City
  Council was unable to recognize them personally, which included “Armenian
  Independence Day” and “Men’s Health Month.”

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Councilmember
  Khan, and unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 2.3 and
  2.7. Consent Calendar Item Nos. 2.1, 2.2, 2.4, and 2.5 were removed to consider
  e-comments submitted by members of the public. Consent Calendar Item No.
  2.6 was removed for separate discussion.

  Following discussion of each removed item, Molly Perry, City Clerk, conducted one
  roll call vote at Mayor Shea’s request to approve the balance of the Consent
  Calendar.

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Vice Mayor Carroll,
  and unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 2.1, 2.2, 2.4,
  2.5, and 2.6.

  2.1  MINUTES

  Chelsea Boyle, Irvine resident, submitted an e-comment expressing
  opposition to invocations at City Council meetings.

  ACTION:
  Approved the minutes of a regular meeting of the Irvine City Council
  held on April 28, 2020.

  2.2  PROCLAMATIONS

  Although an e-comment was submitted on this item, it was deemed by the
  City Attorney to be irrelevant to the agendized subject matter, and
  therefore, not read by the City Clerk.

  ACTION:
  1) Proclaimed May 28, 2020, as "Armenian Independence Day."
  2) Proclaimed June 2020 as "Men's Health Month."

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  May 26, 2020

  2.3  WARRANT AND WIRE TRANSFER RESOLUTION

  ACTION:
  Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 20-39 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, ALLOWING
  CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE
  FUNDS OUT OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID

  2.4  BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS TO CONTRACTED SERVICES FOR THE
  ORANGE COUNTY GREAT PARK

  Susan Sayre, Irvine resident, submitted an e-comment requesting
  clarification between “contracted legal services” and “special legal
  services,” and questioned whether the budget adjustment was a pay
  increase for the City Attorney.

  Mayor Shea noted for the record that that the budget adjustment would not
  result in a salary adjustment, and that the item was simply a reallocation of
  funds, and no increase in contract amount was proposed.

  ACTION:
  1) Approved a budget adjustment (increase) in the amount of
  $45,000 to the contract line for City Attorney Services.
  2) Approved a budget adjustment (decrease) of $45,000 for the
  contract line for Special Legal Services.

  2.5  SENATE BILL 2 GRANTS PROGRAM – PERMANENT LOCAL
  FUNDING ALLOCATION APPLICATION

  Susan Sayre, Irvine resident, submitted an e-comment in support,
  suggesting that the grants and the programs and services, as well as the
  programs that they will be used for, be presented and discussed due to
  increased public interest in affordable housing and housing assistance
  services.

  ACTION:
  Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 20-40 – A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING
  SUBMITTAL OF A GRANT APPLICATION TO THE STATE
  DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
  FOR PROJECTS UTILIZING THE SENATE BILL 2 PERMANENT
  LOCAL HOUSING ALLOCATION FUNDING

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  May 26, 2020

  2.6  DESIGNATION OF AGENT TO EXECUTE CONTRACTS FOR GRANTS
  ADMINISTERED BY THE COUNTY OF ORANGE OFFICE ON AGING

  This item was removed for separate discussion at the request of
  Councilmember Khan, who inquired about whether the City Council would
  have the ability to approve such contracts for grants based on language in
  the resolution designating signature authority to the City Manager.

  Sheila Driscoll, Community Services Manager, responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included requesting that contracts for such grants
  be brought before the City Council for final approval prior to execution.

  ACTION:
  1) Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 20-41 - A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA,
  DESIGNATING AGENT FOR THE PURPOSES OF EXECUTING
  CONTRACTS FOR COUNTY, STATE, AND FEDERAL GRANTS
  FOR PROGRAMS FOR OLDER ADULTS as amended to revise
  Sections 1 and 2 of the resolution as follows:

  SECTION 1. In accordance with the City’s financial
  policies, the City Council of the City of Irvine authorizes the City
  Manager or designee to execute contracts and subsequent
  contract amendments, as well as any other related documents,
  with the County of Orange and/or any of its departments,
  including but not limited to the Office of Aging, to receive grant
  funding on behalf of the City related to older adults.

  SECTION 2. The City Council of the City of Irvine
  authorizes the City Manager or designee to take all actions
  necessary pertaining to grant funding for programs and services
  for older adults administered through the County of Orange
  and/or any of its departments, including but not limited to
  the Office of Aging.

  2) Authorized the City Manager or designee to execute documents
  needed to accept county, state, and federal grants administered
  by the County of Orange Office on Aging.

  2.7  NOTICE OF REVIEW FOR TRACT MAPS IN ORCHARD HILLS

  ACTION:
  Received and filed.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  6
 City Council Minutes  May 26, 2020

  3.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  3.1  APPROVAL OF THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT,
  HOME  INVESTMENT  PARTNERSHIPS,  AND EMERGENCY
  SOLUTIONS GRANT 2020-2021 ACTION PLAN FUNDING
  RECOMMENDATIONS AND THE 2020-2024 CONSOLIDATED PLAN,
  CITIZEN PARTICIPATION PLAN AND ORANGE COUNTY ANALYSIS
  OF IMPEDIMENTS TO FAIR HOUSING CHOICE

  Mayor Shea opened the public hearing at 5:35 p.m.

  Steve Holtz, Manager of Neighborhood Services, and Charles Kovac,
  Housing Administrator, presented the staff report and responded to
  questions. Kevin Trussell, Community Services Commission Chairman,
  also responded to questions and provided a summary of the methodology
  for funding recommendations by the Community Services Commission.

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about qualifications for
  Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDO) funding;
  expressed concern about why certain organizations were overfunded while
  others were underfunded based on their requests; suggested that Irvine
  based organizations be prioritized; discussed the development of funding
  criteria; and inquired about whether all funding recommendations were
  unanimous amongst the Community Services Commission members.

  Councilmember Kuo noted for the record that he was a Boardmember of
  the Irvine Children’s Fund.

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that the following e-comment had been
  received:

  •  Stephanie Schneider, on behalf of StandUp for Kids, expressed
  appreciation for the City Council’s support through CDBG funding
  over the years and consideration of additional funding.

  ACTION: Moved by Vice Mayor Carroll, seconded by Councilmember
  Khan, and unanimously carried to close the public hearing at 6:02
  p.m.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  7

  ACTION: Moved  by  Councilmember  Kuo,  seconded  by
  Councilmember Khan, and unanimously carried to:

  Adopt RESOLUTION NO. 20-42 – A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING
  THE 2020-2024 CONSOLIDATED PLAN, 2020-2021 ACTION
  PLAN, CITIZEN PARTICIPATION PLAN, AND ORANGE COUNTY
  ANALYSIS OF IMPEDIMENTS TO FAIR HOUSING CHOICE FOR
  FEDERAL COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT, HOME
  INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS, AND EMERGENCY SOLUTIONS
  GRANT ENTITLEMENT PROGRAMS

  3.2  APPEALS OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S APPROVAL OF A
  COMMERCIAL MASTER PLAN (00790906-PMPC) AND TRANSFER OF
  DEVELOPMENT RIGHTS AT 2400 BARRANCA PARKWAY IN
  PLANNING AREA 36 (IRVINE BUSINESS COMPLEX)
  Mayor Shea opened the public hearing at 6:05 p.m.

  City Council discussion included: questioning why the item was
  recommended for continuance; and inquired about any potential
  consequences that could ensue as a result of a continuance.

  Tim Gehrich, Deputy Director of Community Development, explained the
  need for the continuance and was available to respond to City Council
  questions.

  ACTION: Moved  by  Councilmember  Kuo,  seconded  by
  Councilmember Khan, and unanimously carried to:

  Continue the public hearing to the June 9, 2020 City Council
  meeting at 4 p.m. or soon thereafter.

  4.  COUNCIL BUSINESS

  4.1  COVID-19 UPDATE

  Mayor Shea noted for the record that she had submitted a memo
